QF.id: AIFM CII Investment Process and Governance_5

question.text: 'Krishna Angel Category I AIF' holds 40,000 convertible preference shares of a start-up, originally issued at INR 25 per share with a conversion ratio of 1:2 (i.e., conversion price INR 50 per equity share). The start-up later issues 20,000 new equity shares at INR 20 per share in a down-round. Under a FULL RATCHET anti-dilution clause, applying the workbook's full-ratchet example mechanics, how many equity shares should the AIF now hold on conversion of its 40,000 preference shares?

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook's full-ratchet example resets the preference-share conversion price to the lowest subsequent issue price and shows that, with a 1:2 conversion ratio, the original count of preference shares converts into the same count of equity shares at the reset price (the worked example converts 30,000 preference shares to 30,000 equity shares, not 60,000). Applying the same mechanics to 40,000 preference shares at issue price INR 25, conversion price INR 50 and reset price INR 20 yields 50,000 equity shares. The Trap: 40,000 ignores the anti-dilution adjustment entirely. 1,00,000 results from doubling for the 1:2 ratio in addition to the price reset, which is inconsistent with the workbook example. 80,000 mis-applies the ratchet using a different price ratio. Note: The full-ratchet and weighted-average examples appear on pages 227-228; the workbook does not state a general formula beyond these worked examples.
